title: inventory-service-discovery-health-probes
content:
Purpose
-----
Notes and working design for the node inventory + service discovery surface used by the routing/control plane across regions. Focus: canonical node catalog schema, GPU labeling conventions, health signal definition and scoring, and how routers consume the catalog for routing decisions and fallbacks in multi-region setups.

Design goals
- Single source of truth for node metadata with low-latency regional caches.
- Deterministic selection for routing that is explainable (why did we pick node X?).
- Cheap, robust health scoring so requests avoid degraded hardware or overloaded nodes.
- Clear GPU naming/typing so model-to-inference mapping can be automated.
- Minimal cross-region sync traffic; eventual consistency acceptable for non-critical fields.

High-level architecture
- Central control plane (multi-master, sharded) holds the canonical registry.
- Each region runs a regional cache (read-through) and a streaming watcher that receives diffs from the control plane.
- Nodes report heartbeats and metrics to a regional agent (push). Agents aggregate, emit health signals to the regional cache and forward rollups to central control plane for historical indexing and fleet analytics.
- Routers consult the regional cache. If no suitable nodes are available, router falls back to peer regions via a policy engine.

Canonical node record (minimal fields)
- node_id: stable UUID (string)
- hostname / ip: (string)
- region: (string) e.g., us-west1
- zone: (string) e.g., us-west1-a
- provider_instance_id: (string) optional
- labels: list of short key:value strings (see label conventions)
- taints: list of short key:value strings (for hard scheduling constraints)
- capacity: cpu_count, memory_gb, gpu_count (strings for compatibility), gpu_types (comma-separated)
- gpu_inventory: comma-separated entries like a100-80gb:2,nvidia-t4:1 (keep as a string in JSON doc store)
- driver_version: string
- free_gpu_mem_mb: numeric string (latest sample)
- last_heartbeat: ISO date string
- health_score: numeric string (0-100)
- readiness_state: ready|draining|offline|maintenance (string)
- created_at, updated_at

Labeling conventions (important for automatic router filters)
Rules: labels are short, stable where possible, and prefixed when they are platform-managed. Human/owner labels should use the "owner:" prefix. Examples: 
- redwood.gpu.family = a100 
- redwood.gpu.memory_gb = 80
- redwood.gpu.count = 4
- redwood.gpu.vendor = nvidia
- redwood.inference.sku = r-infer-a100-80 
- owner:team = solutions-eng
- infra:zone-type = burstable
Notes:
- Use a single label for a canonical SKU (redwood.inference.sku) to make routing rules simpler. 
- Prefer normalized names: a100-80 rather than a100_80 or A100_80G. Avoid slashes.
- Treat GPU driver_version and firmware as capability attributes but not labels (they change frequently).

Health signals and scoring
- Sources: heartbeat (age), CPU load (1m), GPU utilization (avg over 10s/1m), free GPU memory, node temperature, recent OOMs or Xid errors, kernel crashes, scheduler backlog (#pending tasks).
- Poll frequency: agents push heartbeat every 10s; metrics aggregated into 10s windows; health score updated every 30s.
- Health score composition (example):
  - heartbeat_age_ms: 0-100 scaled contribution
  - gpu_util_1m: higher utilization reduces score if > 95%
  - free_gpu_mem_pct: low memory reduces score
  - recent_hard_errors (xid, oom): bring score down immediately to <10
  - scheduling_backlog: moderate weight
  - maintenance_flag: score=0
- The score is kept simple (0-100) so routers can threshold (>=70 preferred, 40-70 warm, <40 avoid).

Health probe types (detailed)
- Heartbeat: node->agent every 10s. If no heartbeat for 30s, mark degraded.
- liveness: agent executes a quick cudaQuery + driver ping every 30s, reports status.
- self-test: scheduled 5m health check that runs a tiny inference micro-benchmark (1-2 tokens) on a pinned model to detect silent failures.
- thermal and power: raw sensors sampled 60s; threshold trips when sustained above safe limits.
- admin override: operator can set readiness_state=maintenance/draining which zeroes routing and sets score to 0-20.

Regional caches & streaming diffs
- Control plane stores canonical records in a strongly-consistent datastore (etcd or cloud RDB).
- Each region maintains an in-memory cache + WAL-backed local DB to survive restarts.
- Updates: nodes -> regional agent -> regional cache -> control plane (write) -> control plane computes compact diffs -> per-region watchers consume diffs via gRPC stream.
- Deltas are compact (field-level) and include tombstones for removals.
- Expiry: if last_heartbeat > 5m, regional cache marks node offline locally without waiting for central. Central cleans up after configured TTL.

Service discovery API (surface)
- GET /nodes?region=us-west1&label=redwood.inference.sku:a100-80&min_health=70&gpu_free_mb>=10240 -> list of node records (paginated)
- Watch API (gRPC): Subscribe to label filters, receive add/update/delete events plus full snapshot on subscription.
- Resolve API for routing (router->control plane): POST /resolve with constraints (region preference, cost tier, required labels, max_latency_ms) returns an ordered candidate list with reason codes.

Router integration and selection algorithm (example flow)
1) Router receives request with model metadata: required_gpu_sku=a100-80, max_latency=50ms, region_hint=us-east1
2) Router queries local regional cache for nodes matching sku and min_health>=70. If count >= batch_size_threshold -> select top N by health_score - estimated_queue_delay.
3) If insufficient nodes, query Resolve API for cross-region candidates, apply network latency penalty (configurable).
4) Apply policy rules: prefer Dedicated pool nodes if workspace has reserved capacity; otherwise prefer cheapest eligible pool that meets latency SLO.
5) Finalize and bind request to chosen node; emit audit event with selection rationale (labels matched, health_score, estimated_cost).

Multi-region considerations
- Node IDs are globally unique. Region-local caches are authoritative for short-term health, central store for long-term metadata.
- Cross-region fallback is policy-driven: prefer same-region, but if insufficient capacity, try peer regions ordered by network latency and cost multiplier.
- Data residency: for Private deployments, catalog entries for on-prem nodes are restricted to that control plane and not advertised publicly.
- Failover tests: periodic canary that routes low-risk jobs cross-region to ensure fallbacks work.

Operational runbook snippets
- On spike in Xid errors: quarantine affected nodes (set readiness_state=maintenance), trigger node_reprovision job, and notify SRE.
- On sudden drop in health_score cluster-wide: check agent ingestion pipeline (Kafka/backfill), verify control plane write latency.
- Node replacement: de-register node in control plane, ensure drains complete, update SKU allocations to avoid capacity overbooking.

Open questions / TODO
- Binary phi for health scoring: should we expose per-model sensitivity to errors (some models more memory-sensitive)?
- Schema evolution: best approach to add GPU features (tensor cores, mig slices) without exploding label count.
- Cost signals: integrate real-time price into routing (spot/preemptible awareness).
- Audit trail size: how long do we store node event history for postmortems? default 90 days?

Appendix: quick example label set for a node
- redwood.inference.sku: r-infer-a100-80
- redwood.gpu.family: a100
- redwood.gpu.memory_gb: 80
- redwood.gpu.count: 4
- infra:zone-type: stable
- owner:team: research

Notes-to-self (short)
- Prototype a tiny service that exposes the Watch API and a simple router consumer; validate latency under 100ms local cache lookups.
- Add unit tests for health_score decay when metrics stop arriving.
- Share with infra-telemetry to align on metric names and tag keys.

End of notes.
